subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Flow Rate and Velocity: Moving the Fluid
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Flow Rate and Velocity: Moving the Fluid.

hook.text: A hydraulic pump moves fluid at a set flow rate. More flow means faster cylinder speed, not more force.

buildup.text: Flow rate is volume per time — liters per minute. It determines how fast actuators move, not how hard they push.

discovery.text: Force comes from pressure. Speed comes from flow. A system with high pressure but low flow lifts heavy loads slowly.

twist.text: Narrow pipes increase fluid velocity but add friction losses. Wider pipes reduce friction but cost more.

climax.text: Engineers size pumps for flow and relief valves for pressure. Getting either wrong wastes energy or breaks things.

punchline.text: Pressure is strength. Flow is speed. They're independent.

quiz.question: What determines the speed of a hydraulic cylinder?
options: The system pressure set by the relief valve
The flow rate of fluid delivered by the pump
The diameter of the hydraulic hoses in the system
